title: Chat docs
intro: Chat is the chat of your own website and admin: a ready chat widget (or your own chat screens on the visitor API), AI replies with your own AI provider key, knowledge, tools, handoff to your staff, an inbox for your admin, leads, flows and reports. Every conversation, message, lead and knowledge entry is kept in your own database (Connections). Your website's tokens are in the Portal: open the website, then Install and tokens. The browser token is public and goes into your pages; the server token is secret and stays on your server.
localhost: Testing on your own computer: the browser token also works on pages served from localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1], on any port, over http or https. These pages use your website's real database, AI key and providers, so the chats made there are real. There is no test mode.
visitorApi: Headless: build your own chat screens on the visitor API with the browser token (Authorization: Bearer). A visitor is a guest or a signed-in Accounts user. The first message of a guest answers guestKey: keep it on the device (localStorage, not cookies or URLs) and send it with every request in the SS-Guest header. A signed-in visitor's Accounts sign-in goes in the SS-Sign-In header; when a device sends both, the guest's chats move to the account (merged by time into the account's own chat when it has one). GET /v1/chat answers the chat and its latest 50 messages; GET /v1/chat?after=<seq> the messages after a sequence number (the new ones), and GET /v1/chat?before=<seq>&limit=<1–50> older ones while earlier is true. Check for new messages from the browser with back-off: every 10 s while the window is open and the tab visible, every 20 s after 5 idle minutes, none after 15 idle minutes or while the tab is hidden, and every 3 s for 45 s while an AI reply is pending (aiPending). POST /v1/chat/messages?wait=1 waits up to 20 s for the AI reply and answers it in replies; a slower reply is still being written (replyPending: true) and comes with the next checks. A reply still pending after 2 minutes shows no typing (aiPending false); the visitor's next check starts it once more, and if it stalls again it counts as failed (fallback answers, else the on-failure setting). There are no websockets.
signedIn: Signed-in chat trusts Accounts sign-ins only: paste your website's Accounts server token into Connections, then pass the visitor's sign-in to the widget with SSChat.identify(token) and call SSChat.identify(null) on sign-out. Chat verifies the sign-in offline with your Accounts public keys. A guest chat that moves to the account takes the name, email and phone it lacks from the sign-in; a merged chat is open when its newest message is the visitor's. Visitors signed in only to your own login chat as guests.
guests: Guests can send a set number of messages per conversation (default 5, 0 = no limit); at the limit they see Sign in to continue (with Signed-in chat and a sign-in page set), Leave your contact and we will reply (with Lead capture) or Message limit reached. A device that sends no guest key starts a new guest. The setting New guests per network (IP) per 15 minutes limits them: n = at most n new guests per network address in 15 minutes, then rate_limited; 0 (the default) = no limit, since many shoppers share one mobile network address. The AI reply limit per network counts guests only, so signed-in visitors are never silenced by others on the same address. Phones a visitor leaves (contact, lead capture, flows, booking) are kept as E.164, read the way every product reads them: a number typed without its country code takes your business.json country's code (with country GB, 07700-900123, 447700900123 and +44 07700 900123 are all +447700900123); without a country, such a number is refused. Claim by phone moves guest chats whose phone is exactly the verified one.
ai: AI replies use your own key: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or any OpenAI-compatible service (base URL and key), with the model you choose, and a backup provider when the main one fails. Answers follow Chat's built-in neutral instructions, your business name and contact from business.json, your own instructions (AI instructions, up to 32,000 characters) and knowledge from the features that are on. AI token caps (daily and monthly, in your business time zone) stop AI replies at the cap; AI cost alerts reach your staff alert recipients once a month when the month crosses the share you set. The language lock makes the AI answer in the visitor's language: its settings set the default language, the marker words (and how many pick a language, or their share of a longer message), how replies are checked (the whole answer, or each part), languages also accepted in Latin letters and the unavailable message in other languages. A reply still in the wrong language after one retry gets the unavailable message in the visitor's language and never hands the chat off by itself (the failures-in-a-row handoff still counts it). An answer may come as several messages (on lines of three dashes, up to the setting), and with the setting a table becomes a message of its own. By default AI replies carry the AI assistant label.
knowledge: The knowledge base holds FAQ entries and articles; website pages are fetched when you add them and when you press Fetch again, never on a schedule. A page that could not be fetched keeps status failed with its reason: http_status (with the httpStatus the page answered) or unreachable; error says the same in English for people. Edit them in the knowledge editor widget or with the server API.
tools: Webhook tools are defined in Settings → Tools (name, description, typed parameters, https URL, and whether to send the signed-in visitor's id and email). The AI may call them; Chat sends each call as a POST with a JSON body { tool, arguments, conversationId, visitor? } and the header ss-chat-signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>"> made with your tool signing secret (Settings → Tools: reveal, copy, regenerate). Calls time out after 8 seconds and at most 64 kB of the answer is read.
booking: Book-a-slot calls your own booking endpoint (Settings → Tools), signed like a tool call, with two requests: { action: "list_slots", from: "YYYY-MM-DD", to: "YYYY-MM-DD", timeZone } answered with { slots: [{ id, start, end }] }, and { action: "book", slotId, name, email, phone, conversationId } answered with { booked: true, reference? }.
handoff: Handoff moves a chat to a person: the visitor asks (button or phrases), a keyword matches, the AI decides, or the AI fails a number of times in a row. The chat is flagged Waiting for a person and the AI stops until a staff member replies or hands the chat back to the AI (resuming the AI: Hand back to the AI in the inbox, PUT /v1/conversations/<id>/ai with paused false, or aiPaused false). Outside your office hours the visitor is told when staff are back. A guest with no contact details is asked for them. Reassurance and the queue position count from the latest handoff (waitingSince).
flows: Flows are short scripted step lists (message, question with buttons, collect a field, hand off, end), started by a page rule (the widget starts them when the chat opens on a matching page, or after the delay) or by a keyword in a visitor message. Path patterns: an exact path, * = one segment, ** = any (for example /products/**).
alerts: Staff alerts, AI cost alerts, transcripts and reply alerts are sent through Notifications: paste your website's Notifications server token into Connections. They go out with Chat's default words (US English) by email and SMS until you write your own templates in Notifications (Settings → Templates, where you can also switch a message off on a channel); WhatsApp has no default words, so it needs your WhatsApp template approved at Meta. Staff alerts and cost alerts go to the recipients setting (email addresses get email; phone numbers WhatsApp, or SMS with the setting Phones get) and, with the setting Also alert Accounts staff who can, to every unblocked Accounts user whose role may reply in the inbox (inbox.reply) or, with all_staff, may see the inbox (inbox.read) (Accounts token); new message and Chat needs you alerts also go to the assigned person; a message Notifications did not take is tried again on the website's next uses for up to a day. Transcripts are emails; without the token they answer notifications_not_connected. Reply alerts go when staff reply to a visitor who has not checked the chat for the away time, once until they check again, by the setting Channels, in order (email, SMS and WhatsApp; WhatsApp, then email by default): the first channel the visitor has an address for (a phone for SMS and WhatsApp), and when Notifications does not take it there (that channel is off, has no template or is switched off for the message), the next one; with none chosen no alert is sent. Alerts link to your Inbox address with ?conversation=<id>, or with the id where the address has {id}. Staff alert values: visitor, name, preview (140 characters on one line), message (the visitor's latest message, up to 500 characters with its line breaks), phone (with the setting Alerts carry the visitor's phone), link, conversationId and business. A transcript carries the most recent 1,000 characters of the chat (the longest value Notifications takes).
attachments: Attachments go from the browser straight to your own S3-compatible storage with a short presigned PUT that fixes the type and size; Chat keeps only the object key. Allow your website's origin (and your admin's) in the bucket's CORS: methods PUT and GET, header content-type. Images (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF) show inline; PDFs are downloads, or open in a new tab with the setting Open PDFs in the browser. Visitors may send only those (with the setting Visitors may attach: everyone, or signed-in visitors only); staff may also send Word, Excel and text files, always as downloads. Attachment links are Chat's own (/v1/files/…): each use sends the browser on to a fresh 10-minute link in your storage, so the links of a chat left open keep working. The largest file is a setting: for visitors default 5 MB, at most 10 MB; for staff default 10 MB, at most 100 MB.
dataRights: Data rights: paste this website's Chat server token into Accounts. Export returns a person's conversations (with their messages and attachments' names) and leads; delete removes them, guest chats merged into the account included. Chat never deletes conversations because of their age; you delete them with DELETE /v1/conversations/<id>.
activity: Activity log: every staff action through the widgets or the server API (reply, note, status, assignment, knowledge edits …) is kept in your database and copied to Accounts when its token is pasted: who (with their role), what, the target with its label (the visitor's name, an entry's or saved reply's title), a short detail such as Status: open → resolved, and when — never message contents. Read it with GET /v1/activity (below).
serverApi: In Chat: the lists of GET and PUT /v1/lists/<list> are tools (Webhook tools), flows (Flows), custom_fields (Custom fields) and page_rules (Page rules), each the whole list in { value }, checked as in Settings. Conversations count with GET /v1/conversations/count and GET /v1/conversations/counts?by=status|waiting|guest|unread, with the list's own filters (status, waiting=1, visitor=guest|user, assigned=unassigned|me, q); waiting, guest (the visitor is a guest) and unread (visitor messages no one on your staff opened) count as true and false. The inbox widget's twins are GET /v1/admin/conversations/count and /counts (inbox.read). Replies, status changes, assignment and knowledge edits made with the server token and SS-Actor headers carry that person's name (on the message, as staffId and name, and in the activity log with their role), add them to the staff list, and assigned=me means them; without the headers they show as Team. A visitor call from your server sends the guest's key in SS-Guest or the visitor's sign-in in SS-Sign-In, and SS-Visitor-IP: the AI reply limits per network count by that address.
shop: Shop tools, track shipment and product cards read your shop in Ecommerce: paste this website's Ecommerce server token into Connections. Each tool is offered to the AI only while its feature is on: Shop tools: product search and details (search_catalog, get_product_details), deals and savings quotes (quote_product_savings, list_active_deals), top and new products (get_top_products), my orders and account (get_my_orders, get_my_account) and Track-shipment (track_shipment). My orders, account and track shipment are offered only to a visitor whose Accounts sign-in Chat verified on that request; Chat forwards that sign-in to Ecommerce in the SS-Sign-In header, and Ecommerce verifies it itself and answers only that user's data (never full street addresses or phone numbers). The AI never chooses the user, the website or the token. When Ecommerce cannot answer (token missing or refused, Ecommerce stopped or unreachable), the AI says it cannot look this up right now and everything else keeps working. These are the Ecommerce routes Chat calls with the pasted token (server token; Ecommerce implements exactly these):
install: Add the script to the pages of your website. The chat widget mounts itself; it renders nothing while Visitor chat is off, the product is stopped, or your database is not connected.
admin: Admin widgets run in your own admin with a ticket: Inbox (inbox.read to see conversations and set your presence, inbox.reply to reply and attach, inbox.manage for status, assignment, notes, saved replies, custom field values and max chats), Knowledge editor (knowledge.edit) and Reports (reports.read). The inbox setting Guest chats in the inbox shows every chat, guest chats only once handed to a person, or signed-in visitors' chats only (in the list, its counts and the unread badge); pausing the AI needs inbox.manage, or inbox.reply with the setting Pausing the AI needs. Hand back to the AI resumes the AI in a chat waiting for a person. A chat can be assigned to anyone on the staff list, or to an Accounts user whose role may reply in the inbox (with the Accounts token); with Assign automatically set to first replier, an unassigned chat goes to the first member of staff who replies. Include the script without data-token, place the widgets and register your ticket function. The widget calls it at start and 1 minute before the ticket expires; your server checks the user's sign-in and role every time. SSChat.onUnread(callback) gives the unread count for your own menu; the server can read it with GET /v1/inbox/unread.
tickets: Your server asks for a ticket with the server token (never send the server token to a browser). The origin is the address of your admin page: any https origin, or a local one while testing. Tickets last 15 minutes and carry only the permissions of switched-on features.
business: Every product reads your business basics from https://<your domain>/.well-known/business.json. Only name is required; without the file the name is your domain and the time zone is UTC.
api: Every API route answers JSON (204: no body); errors are RFC 9457 problems with a stable code. Lists are paged with cursor and limit. Routes of a feature that is off answer 403 feature_off. The reference below says what each call takes and answers.
cards: Product cards: the products search_catalog, get_product_details and get_top_products return (up to the setting Products per search per answer: default 5, at most 12) show under the AI answer as cards with the image, the name linking to the product page, the price and Add to cart. Add to cart dispatches the cancelable window event ss-ecommerce:add-to-cart with detail { productId, variantId, quantity: 1 }. Ecommerce's widget on the same page adds the item to its cart and calls preventDefault(); when no widget does, the card opens the product page instead. Your own cart can listen for the same event. Every word on a card is a widget text (Settings, Texts).
contextPanel: Context panel shop info: with the Ecommerce token pasted and a signed-in visitor, the inbox's context panel also shows the visitor's last 5 orders (number, status, total) and loyalty points, read from Ecommerce with the server token; for guests, or without the token, it shows nothing about the shop.
import: Import (server token only, feature Import): move staff, guests, conversations and their messages in from another system with ss-import, or with your own script on the import routes. POST /v1/import/<collection> takes NDJSON (application/x-ndjson, one record per line, at most 1,000 records or 4 MB per call) in Chat's own shapes: staff { id, name, email?, presence?, maxChats?, createdAt? }; guests { keyHash, id, expireAt?, createdAt? }, where keyHash is the SHA-256 (hex) of the old guest cookie value, so a guest's chats keep working through the store's own cookie sent as SS-Guest; conversations with their given ids (visitor, contact, status, waiting, AI pause, assignment, note, custom field values, summary, rating, the page it started on, unread counts, lastMessageAt, createdAt); and messages { id, conversationId, author, staffId?, name?, text, format?, internal?, attachment?, createdAt }, one record per message, after their conversations. Times are ISO 8601 with a zone. Each record is written by its key and replaced when it is there already, so a re-run gives exactly the source again; unknown fields and the tenant fields are refused by name, and text longer than Chat keeps is refused, never cut. ?dryRun=1 checks without writing. Then call POST /v1/import/finish (again with ?after=<next> while more is true): it numbers each imported conversation's messages 1..n by time and derives its counters, preview and read marks. POST /v1/import/<collection>/prune removes imported records the source no longer has (records made in Chat itself stay), and GET /v1/import/status answers the counts and the sums ss-import verify compares. An import sends nothing: no message, event, alert, AI call or activity copy.
